scenarios.acceptance: Commit ingress before HTTP 202; inject failure after each command/operation/idempotency write and immediately before commit, proving all-or-none records. Lose the response after commit and replay the same idempotency key, returning the same operation without duplicate commands.
State, inbox, outbox and owning operation commit together; injected failure leaves no partial domain update.
The same object ID in another business/project/client cannot be read, linked, leased or acknowledged using the caller scope.
Expired lease epoch and stale object revision cannot commit; database time controls leases.
Two subscriptions independently receive and acknowledge one stable message ID.
A downstream projection failure does not reopen a succeeded originating operation.
Unknown commit response is reconciled from idempotency/inbox/operation state before retry; external effects are never blindly replayed.
Workers and Containers exchange durable messages, not application-handler RPC; memory, waitUntil and transport notifications cannot certify the buffer.

Revoked membership is denied at execution and every read; a body principal or scope cannot replace trusted context. SQL metacharacters remain bound values, dynamic identifiers are allowlisted, and arbitrary client SQL is rejected.
Database URL/token are server-only environment references; logs and public bundles never contain token values.
Worker rejects native filesystem/SQLite bindings; unsupported new-Turso vs libSQL transport is rejected, never silently coerced.
Stopping/restarting a Container or terminating an isolate leaves durable pending work recoverable within its retry budget.
Browser memory/OPFS/IndexedDB/cache and ephemeral container disk do not satisfy server durable_async; local persistence is not authorization or backup.
